properties.name: Las Palmas - Mindelo, Day 1
properties.description: We are off! The atmosphere is interesting, somehow everyone is calm and silent, not much talking. Somehow we all know we are embarking on something special, but for me it feels like any other sailing trips I’ve done.  The leaving and fueling up works smoothly, I’m glad that Mark is giving instructions calm and not nervously. Because Al told me that often in such a bit stressful situations, the true spirit of a crew is visible.  As soon as we leave the harbor, the waves get noticeably higher. The spray even sometimes comes into the cockpit. We set the sails quite quickly, second reef and the wind speeds of around 18-20 knots push us nicely southwards. Bruce the weather guy told us to first head towards south-east, to avoid the lee of the islands. Rika and Matty quickly get a bit seasick and head down to the cabin to nap. Luckily my patch is working and I feel superb! No seasickness and really enjoying the waves.  Dinner: Curry by Mark

properties.name: Las Palmas - Mindelo, Day 2
properties.description: In the evening Mark cooks a really nice curry, which we eat with the left over rice. The waves are still high, we would estimate around 3-4m. But it’s impressive to observe them.  The night was a bit rough, I kept waking up every 45min because of the rolling of the boat. Rika was quite sick and had to throw up several times. So we divided the night shifts between three, Mark joined all of us for some time. Mine is 3:00-7:00. At 4:00 we jibe and set towards a westerly course. The wind calms down a bit and everything goes smooth.  I have a bit a heavy breathing, not sure if it’s asthma or anxiety. But it’s not strong and when I talk with someone it goes away.  At the end of my shift I get tired and wake up Matty at 7, eat a bread with jam and go to sleep for another 4h. This time I sleep better and wake up fresh.  Rika and Matty feel better and are out in the cockpit. I take my first shower on the boat, it feels awesome! I still feel so comfortable and all the worries I had the last few days are gone. I’m quite happy living on this small floating thingy for the next three weeks. But I also have trouble grasping or understanding the length of this trip.  Dinner: Pasta Bolognese by Dan

properties.name: Las Palmas - Mindelo, Day 3
properties.description: I was very happy cooking dinner and managed without any seasickness. But when I tried to defrost the meat in the microwave, the whole power supply collapsed and the autopilot stopped working. Rob was shouting from the helm for help because he couldn’t see where the wind was coming from. I tried to give him directions and we managed to get the boat on course again, but not after a few circles and unwanted jibes. In the meantime Mark put the power back on and we could calm down again.  After the dinner Mark insisted on doing the washing up and wouldn’t let anyone help him. We had a beautiful sunset and then I already went to bed quickly. I tried to watch some Netflix (Rita) but got a bit dizzy and decided to sleep.  When muy shift started around 4am, the wind has shifted and came from the back. Since we already went too much north instead of south, Mark and me did a Chinese jibe together, which means to turn the boat the other way about 290° and therefore actually doing a tack.  All of a sudden an alarm signal came on, but only around ever minute. Mark investigated and found out that it’s the bilge pump isn’t working. This is quite a crucial pump, which removes water from the boat in case of a leak. Since it wasn’t working since quite some time probably, some water has collected. We alternated in manually pumping it out, with the emergency pump.  After 7 I slept again around 4 hours and woke up fresh and happy around lunchtime. Mark and Rob started to work on replacing the bilge pump, which luckily Mark had a spare of. It was very successful and after around 2h everything was working again. Also the waves and wind have calmed down and it was smooth sailing. Just when I went to the bow for the first time, the dolphins came and stayed for quite some time. I enjoyed watching them sooooo much.  Dinner: Fajitas by Mark

properties.name: Las Palmas - Mindelo, Day 4
properties.description: Well what a plot twist. Yesterday just before dinner, the plotter started to restart every other minute. Mark immediately started to investigate, but it got worse and worse. Ever minute all the power of the boat shut down, came on again for a moment and just going off again. Around 7:00 all the power was dead. Mark was dumbfounded and couldn’t figure out at all what could be the issue. We started to realize what this means:  no autopilot  no lights  no navigation system  no emergency satellite communication (SkyMate)  no VHF (apart from the handheld)  no charging for the phones/laptops  no fridge  no freezer  no waterpump (luckily there is a manual one in the kitchen)  no gas, because the switch is managed electrically  no engine to motor  No generator  No showers  No hot water  No windlass : no anchoring  But we also realized that we still can sail and use the compass and the wind pointer for navigation. Also Marks iPad had a backup plotter which we can use. Also there is a backup burner for the kitchen.  So we can advance and cook our food, which are the most important things. We decided to change the course towards Mindelo on Capo Verde, which was still 560nm away, 4-5 days sailing. Our main worry was that the family and friends were expecting daily updates on our location through SkyMate. If they don’t hear from us for the next 4 days, they will be worried to death.  Nevertheless we went into action mode and decided on 2h shifts with two people, which means you would only get around 2h if sleep between each shift. None of us could really sleep because of the fear and adrenaline. Additionally the navigation was quite difficult without the system and we made around 10 accidental jibes, which means that the boom is thrown to the other side with a loud swoooosh and boom. This always woke everyone up and could seriously damage the rigging if it continues. We also sometimes moved in circles, confused about what our course is. This night no one slept well, also the waves and the wind were pretty strong.  In the morning the waves were still high and strong, but eased down a bit after some time. We finally took down the main sail which took some damage over the night. I cooked some porridge with the spare camping stove Mark has on board. Then we tried to start fixing the electricity issue. We decided that SkyMate is the most important component on board, so my idea was to find its power input and connect it directly to the batteries, which still had power. It was quite the task to crawl around on the bottom of the boat trying to follow wire and see where it’s connected to. Finally we found the right one and I could directly put into action the things I learned from Al. I cut the wire and attached it to some clamps, which I could directly put to the batteries. It took some time then to find the spot with 12V difference, because the batteries are split into 4 units. But finally we found one, attached the clamps and screamed in joy when the little lights of the unit lit up! Immediately we checked the connection and had already three new messages sitting in our inbox. What a success! We informed the important people that everything’s alright and that we’re heading now to Mindelo.  In the afternoon it eased and everybody’s spirit got higher again. We put on music and Rika and I had a little crochet session. Then the dolphins came and stayed for several hours which was amazing. They were jumping around all sides of the boat and spread really good mood. We started to joke and say that we’re having the best time.  Dinner: Fried Rice with chicken by Mark

properties.name: Las Palmas - Mindelo, Day 5
properties.description: But of course this didn’t last long. At night around 11 we got an update from the weather guy Bruce which predicted unpleasant conditions up ahead. We will directly cross the trade wind surge, which he originally wanted us to go around. The wind will be around 35 knots and waves to up to 3.5-4m high. This is still not a storm and manageable with the boat but will just make the next days much harder. And indeed when I went to sleep, the rocking and throwing around made it impossible to sleep. In addition to that my head started to go in overdrive and envision all the bad things that could happen now. Every creaking sound or splash made me worried. I was scared and started to feel quite some anxiety. The resulting sleep deprivation made it even worse. I think that night I only slept around 3h. But at least whenever I was up in the cockpit I felt better, seeing the sea and being able to steer made me feel better and in control. During the day I tried to sleep more but still couldn’t. It was wrecking. I just wanted to arrive to Mindelo.  Dinner: Meatballs with thawed veggies in a wrap by Rika.

properties.name: Las Palmas - Mindelo, Day 6
properties.description: Yesterday evening when I couldn’t nap I felt terrible, but after some food I was ready to do the first night shift together with Rika. We listened to a True Crime podcast together which made the shift go by very quickly and quite pleasant. Then I tried to sleep but still couldn’t. So Mark offered me to take my next shift and I took a sleeping pill which knocked me out and I finally slept for 6 hours. Then I replaced Rob and did a 6 hour shift into the morning. When sitting down at the wheel, I noticed a flying fish on deck! They are very interesting creatures. The sun came up and I felt much better and went down to make scrambled eggs for everyone.  Since we didn’t have an automatic bilge pump anymore, I kept checking it regularly. I always filled up a bit and there was also some water collecting under my bed. Every time we sponged it up, it filled again gradually and it made me a bit worried. The same for the bilge, which never stayed empty and needed pumping like 2-3 times a day.  Around 2pm tried to nap a bit and actually managed to sleep two hours which made me quite happy. The seasickness patch wasn’t working anymore so I took it off. I felt some effects of the seasickness but not that strongly and could be dealt with well with the occasional pill.  Another thing we started to notice today was that the steering wheels made a strange cracking sound. It slowly started to become more and we already talked about the possibility of needing to use the emergency tiller. I hope it won’t be needed until we arrive in Mindelo.  The coast guard in Mindelo responded to our email and said that they are on standby and awaiting our arrival, which was a great relieve! They wanted regular position updates, which made me feel much safer. In case something else happens they would know where to search.  After dinner we all sat in the cockpit, watching the sunset and having pleasant conversations. I realized how glad I was that everyone was looking after each other and in general what a great team we were. And it wasn’t just born out of friendship or personal care for each other, it was more the fact that we’re all in the same boat and needed to work together. But also I felt how this situation made us get closer to everyone.  Dinner: Steak with thawed veggies in a wrap by Mark

properties.name: Las Palmas - Mindelo, Day 7
properties.description: The weather calmed down a bit and we settled in for another night watch. We jibed again and found a really great course that worked with the wind and will bring us more or less directly to Mindelo. Helming was rather easy and the waves pushed us nicely. I did two night shifts, one with Rob and one with Mark and we had really nice and deep conversation. However, when going to sleep after the second watch I had quite a strong anxiety attack and had trouble breathing. I took an seasickness pill, then a Temesta and also CBD oil. I then managed to sleep but just around 4-5h and the breathing issues continued. I went in the cockpit, told Rob and Mark that I’m not doing well and they were quite understanding. I played the guitar and sang which helped a lot. The day then was okay, I managed distract myself enough so that the symptoms were not too strong.  Rob and I managed to connect a USB plug to the batteries, so that we can charge our phones and headlamps. I really enjoyed the work, even though I got quite a bit seasick since my patch didn’t work anymore. We had a great dinner, and then I played a bit more guitar. I was scared of going to bed and have another anxiety attack. Right now I’m laying in bed and hope I can rest a bit. In 1.5h I have my shift together with Rika and we will listen to a True Crime podcast, which I’m already looking forward to. Worst case I just don’t sleep tonight, because tomorrow evening we will finally arrive in Mindelo, Capo Verde! I’m soooo excited and happy to finally see land and feel more safe again, I’ve been under quite some adrenaline and a pressure the last 5 days. Tomorrow will be a good day!

properties.name: Las Palmas - Mindelo, Day 8
properties.description: We arrived. We made it, we are safe. It was a hell of a trip in the end. First of all the wind slowed down and we took much longer than anticipated. Then when we tried to call the Marina, which via Email agreed to help us, but they didn’t answer. We were making circles in the bay and trying to reach anyone who could help us. We had just one sail, no electricity and no engine so we needed to be towed to a safe harbor. In the end we called 112 and a nice police guy started to organize help. It tool around 2 hours and almost running against a cliff until finally some people in a motor boat arrived and circled the boat. Communication was very difficult, they barely spoke English and we didn’t speak Portuguese. When all the wind died down they finally threw us a rope and started towing. But instead to the Marine they brought us to a massive industrial dock and during the process of docking we almost crashed. There was a lot of shouting and screaming and there were around 5 police men waiting for us. When we finally secured the boat, I immediately fell into a deep sleep.  The next morning I woke up after just 5h and couldn’t go back to sleep anymore. I made myself some scrambled eggs and enjoyed sitting on land. Then I went to search some wifi, found it in a nearby bar and immediately called my mom. The first thing I saw was her worried expression because she didn’t expected to hear from me for another two weeks! Hearing her voice suddenly made me quite emotional and all of a sudden I started to cry. It felt good to release some pressure.

He was working in forestry and he was about to let the tree fall on him, but then the tree fell to the other side. He said that since then he never wanted to fall in love madly at all, and he advises everybody to always stay distant and stay cold. He says he’s very afraid of falling in love too much. He got together with the sister of his ex to get back on her, which was a mistake he said. He got a kid with her and now the mom is sick with cancer and in her last months. They are separated now. He started to have panic attacks so he went to the psychiatrist and he’s taking medication now and is feeling better. The medication and the therapist are really expensive though. He said he didn’t used to believe in panic attack but now he does. He seems to be a great dad. He takes his kid out on the countryside to go horseback riding. And back in the valley somewhere starts the land of her grandfather. Also drove us 5min further to the beach, where she said we can camp with no problems.

properties.name: Beach Puerto Ibanez
properties.description: Amazing spot next to a blue lake

properties.name: Carretera Austral
properties.description: Decided to take the bus since it was raining a lot

properties.name: Camping Chile Chico
properties.description: Chill camping in town, it was raining

properties.name: Middle of nowhere
properties.description: Going to work on a construction site close to the border. Took us a bit futher, to the middle of nowhere.

properties.name: Camping Chile Chico
properties.description: Family from somewhere close to Buenos Aires. Saved us from the rain which started suddenly and we didn’t have raincovers and no roof. We decided to go back, since there were no cars and rain, and also the entrance to the valle lunar is closed after 2pm.

properties.name: Puerto Ibanez
properties.description: Went back because we had a rental car soon

properties.name: Beach Puerto Ibanez
properties.description: Spent an amazing afternoon here, fishing a big fish and just enjoying the good weather

properties.name: Balmaceda
properties.description: We were in a rush to get to the airport to get the rental car. We were already late and no cars stopped. Then Andres saved us, and as a coincidence he also worked for the same rental company! Nice guy, speaks German quite well because he lived in the Canary Islands for some years with a German family and also had many German friends. Very impressive tho. Was nice to have his number in case something happens with the rental car.

properties.name: Cerro Castillo River
properties.description: Decided to take a rental car for the last week of Karims visit. We met Natalia again with her brother Andres.

properties.name: Lago General Carrera
properties.description: Great spot next to the lake, cover from a tree. Played a lot of Tichu

properties.name: Puerto Bertrand
properties.description: Amazing spot, just next to the very blue river, just difficult to get up again with a 2x4, but doable

properties.name: Laguna Esmeralda
properties.description: Small peninsula next to a mirador, great spot

properties.name: Caleta Tortel
properties.description: Felt like the end of the world

properties.name: Parque Nacional Patagonia
properties.description: Spent the night in the park in the hope to see Pumas, which we did in the morning!

properties.name: Puerto Bertrand
properties.description: Spent another night at this great spot, but it was raining like crazy. But had a cosy evening in my tent playing Tichu, it was Natalias birthday

properties.name: Camping El Blanco
properties.description: Last evening with Karim, it was raining and soooo cold

properties.name: Balmaceda
properties.description: Time to say goodbye to Karim

properties.name: Coyhaique
properties.description: two older guys working in construction

properties.name: Villa Amengual
properties.description: alm and funny older guy. He owns a tourism company. But really humble and friendly. Told me this crazy story of when he have he finished high school. He just took a bag went to Buenos Aires and started working on ships as a marine. He he found a job on the first boat and left the next day to Japan. He worked as this for 12 years and also got married meanwhile, every time he came back there was another baby. They are still married now more than 50 years. He kept making jokes that he’s so old he’s from the Neanderthal age and he got married with a stick. He also ended up picking up another 3 hitchhikers with who I spent the night with, Dani, Seba y Juan

properties.name: Villa Amengual
properties.description: Met these guys hitchhiking. Climbed over a fence, it was raining and cold. Then the owner came when he have already set up the tents. He was pissed but let us stay in the end

properties.name: Cruze to Puerto Cicnes
properties.description: Funny guy, going to work in Puerto Cicnes. Was really happy about me knowing some Chilenan words. Told me about Coigüe, the native tree

properties.name: Cascada el condor
properties.description: I waited for 2h in the cold, had wet feet, so at some point I decided to walk one hour to this waterfall

properties.name: La Junta
properties.description: quien anda en patagonia apurado, pierde su tiempo! Never saw someone drive that slow, drove reeeeally cautious and had a queue behind him. Also stopped a lot to take pictures. Offered me some coffee which was great since I was waiting for 3h in the cold and rain before.

properties.name: Villa Santa Lucia
properties.description: Truck driver, but also drives buses and the ambulance! First picked up Lukas, another German hitchhiker and then also me.

properties.name: Lago Yuelche
properties.description: Originally from Chile but his parents fled to Argentina when he was 1 years old because they were supporters of Allende. Talked about Colonia Dignidad which was very interesting, apparently there is another documentary about finding Schäfer in Argentina.

properties.name: Lago Yuelche
properties.description: Camped with another hitchhiker at this amazing beach, with amazing view of the lake and the mountains. Calm night

properties.name: Chaiten
properties.description: Sweet couple from Osorno, here on vacation. Also ended up picking up Lukas as well, he already left earlier.

properties.name: Caleta Gonzalo
properties.description: young dad with several negocios and a piece of land with animals. Chill and fun, but he’s a dad of two girls and kept talking about the pretty Swiss girls. Also told me how he trapped and killed a Puma that threatened his animals.

properties.name: Picholco
properties.description: Nice ferry ride, amazing wifi

properties.name: Contao
properties.description: The same guy brought me to my camping spot

properties.name: Contao
properties.description: Nice calm spot, found a small spot hidden from the wind

properties.name: Puelche
properties.description: Brought me to the ferry, at first was a bit suspicious but then really nice

properties.name: Puerto Montt
properties.description: Asked around on the ferry, they were also not so sure at the beginning, but then really talkative and nice.

properties.name: Renting a room
properties.description: Took a room for a night in a house with a local family

properties.name: Gasolinera Puerto Montt
properties.description: Traveling with Jordan now, getting to a good place for hitchhiking

properties.name: Pargua
properties.description: Really nice guy, brought us all across the ferry to Chiloe. He works in a salmonera. When saying goodbye, he gifted us 6 small salmons, for sure around 1kg of fish. This evening we ate a lot of fish

properties.name: Chacao
properties.description: The ferry is free

properties.name: Linao
properties.description: Construction workers, working on the renovation of the ruta 5. They are the reason for the big delays of the main route and why everyone is going along the coast instead.

properties.name: Playa Huelden
properties.description: A doctor, he’s going to Chiloe just temporarily, because there are not enough doctors here.

properties.name: Random beach
properties.description: Nice calm beach, the locals immediately pointed us to the place where to camp.

properties.name: Mocopulli
properties.description: Brought us directly to the campground where we planned to hide out the strong rain that was coming in.  The campground had no camping spots left but had a refugio for people on foot or bike for the same price.

properties.name: Curaco de Velez
properties.description: We asked before the ferry and they said yes. Dad and son, very fun. Said if you do a favor, you have to do it right. So he stopped at some nice spots for pictures and even drove a different road with nicer views.

properties.name: Anchao
properties.description: Picked us up just when it started to rain. Left us at a bus stop to continue hitchhiking

properties.name: Mirador
properties.description: Young guy studying in concepcion, back home for the vacation.  Then slept at the mirador to have some roof, nice views

properties.name: Quinchao
properties.description: Sweet couple on vacation here on the island of Quinchao

properties.name: South of Quinchao
properties.description: Back of a pickup truck, when we got out without even asking she told us about a great beach to camp, where there are many birds and also fresh water. It was exactly what we were looking for

properties.name: Playa Mallil
properties.description: Such calm beach, nothing happening, many birds, lots of blackberries, awesome sunset

properties.name: Anchao
properties.description: Offered us a shower at his place and even came to get us with his car. Really nice and respectful guy, told us about the tradition of the Jesus de Nazareo where they make a rowing competition from one island to the other.

properties.name: Chonchi
properties.description: What an amazing woman, loved her. Very independent and strong, often travels alone. But she says she is very careful going about it, she would never hitchhike. She had three cats that she loves, they are called Lolo, Lala, Lulu, and amazingly her veteranaria is called Lola

properties.name: Huillinco
properties.description: He said they also call him “El chocolate”. I had a bad feeling going into the car and the whole ride, not sure why. But the car was so broken, the windshield was just barely holding together.

properties.name: Playa Huillinco
properties.description: We first tried to camp more south, but the unfriendly neighbor said he would call the police, so we went more up the beach and crossed the little river on foot. There we found a perfect spot, with lots of grass, it’s part of a salmoneria apparently. Also great for swimming.

properties.name: Cucao
properties.description: Belgian couple speaking French, traveling in Chile. They had a very fancy rental car.

properties.name: Playa Cucao
properties.description: Just a short distance, they were going to the beach and helped us to walk a few kilometer less

properties.name: On the way to Cole Cole
On the way to Cole Cole
properties.description: Pickup

properties.name: Playa Cole Cole
properties.description: One of the most beautiful beaches, amazing sunset, small campground administered by the indigenous community of the Mapuche. Small picknick tables right next to the sea with trees for hammocks.

properties.name: On the way to Cole Cole
Cucao
properties.description: Pickup

properties.name: Casone Huillinco
properties.description: Nice guy, don’t remember much of the conversation unfortunately.

properties.name: Huillinco
properties.description: So hard to hitchhike, walked a long time

properties.name: Casona Huillinco
properties.description: After waiting for a loooong time for someone to pick us up, and walking almost an hour they picked us up and decided to also drive us back to the festival. Fun guys, one of them from Venezuela, we offered them two beers as a thank you.

properties.name: Casona Huillinco Festival
properties.description: Went to a small festival in the woods and could sleep next to the lake

properties.name: Huillinco
properties.description: Older women, who used to work as a surveyor like me for 40 years. She told me how the job changed over the years with electrical distance measuring and GPS. She worked in all Chile, always for around 2-3 weeks, going to very remote places. I would love to work as this one day. But after 40 years she had enough and now helps her husband with his business with seafood.

properties.name: Chonchi
properties.description: Pickup

properties.name: Castro
properties.description: Cute couple from Quellon, going to Castro for shopping

properties.name: Playa Ahui
properties.description: Very, very friendly and chill guy, I saw him at the gas station and thought I could go over and ask. He immediately said yes. Since he was almost going to the place we wanted to go the day after, we decided to change plans and go there immediately. He even drove us around 10min further.

properties.name: Playa Ahui
properties.description: Calm beach, no problem to camp, space for hammock

properties.name: Somewhere
properties.description: After waiting for a long time, a couple picked us up and it turns out they are the owners of Chilota, the cute dog that accompanied us all day and night.

properties.name: Somewhere
properties.description: No cars

properties.name: Chiloe Silvester
properties.description: A pickup picked us up, turns out they also go to the same animal sanctuary.

properties.name: Carretera
properties.description: The same family in the pickup brought us to the main road

properties.name: Ancud
properties.description: After waiting for some time with not many cars, all of a sudden the same family in the pickup appeared again and brought us all the way to Ancud

properties.name: Playa Ancud
properties.description: three guys here for work. They are staying in some cabanas outside of the town and brought us to the campspot. Fun guys

properties.name: Playa Ancud
properties.description: Many mosquitos, but nice sunset

properties.name: Chacao
properties.description: Hitchhiking the three of us, with Jordan and Oscar. Señor de las ostras, has a big business with oysters with around 30 employees. Told us about the option to find a passage on a cargo boat going south.

properties.name: Pargua
properties.description: Works in a salmonera, brought us a little way to the next town. He said he tries to always spend one hour each day to do something nice for someone, so this day it was us.

properties.name: Camping Ceiba
properties.description: Truck driver, said he can only take one person in the front, so Jordan and me went in the back, which was a closed off box. It was dark but comfortable, by a small hole in the wall we could see a projection of the outside world passing by, like a camera oscura. He did a detour just to let us out right next to the campground.

properties.name: Home Benjamin
properties.description: A guy I met on an app, offered to host me. When I said that I am with two other travelers, he said that’s no problem he can take us all. Turns out to be an amazing experience, we stayed for many days exactly when the bad weather with thunderstorms and much rain for days rolled in. He works as an software engineer in a salmora, has a cute dog which is soooo shy, and lived alone in a small wooden house on the outskirts of the town. He did way too much for us, always offering us food and driving us around.

properties.name: Home Gabito <3
properties.description: Stayed three nights at the house of Gabo and Nafe

properties.name: Puerto Montt Salida
properties.description: Started hitchhikign to Ushuaia with Oscar

properties.name: Puerto Montt Salida
properties.description: Small trip, asked us if we were from Israel. He told us she would not take people from Israel in her car because the probability is just too high that they are bad travelers. Very often there are not respectful and stealing things

properties.name: Chamiza
properties.description: amazing woman really nice vibe. She is a psychologist and sexologist. She immediately invited us to her home to stay, but we wanted to continue traveling.

properties.name: La Arena
properties.description: The same guy that picked me up in Contao a few weeks ago. What a coincidence!

properties.name: Puelche
properties.description: The ferry is free

properties.name: Hornopiren
properties.description: - Very nice couple from Santiago, on a roadtrip down the carretera austral. We asked them at the ferry and they agreed to take us to Hornopiren. Told us about the bread made from corn, called Churrasca.

properties.name: Fjordo Largo
properties.description: I asked around at the entrance to the ferry about someone who can take me the small part between the two ferries. He accepted and we had a nice chill ride.

properties.name: Mirador Lago Rio Negro
properties.description: We were able to continue with them up to the place to camp. It was their first night in the tent and we had coffee together in the morning.

properties.name: Chaiten
properties.description: We could continue even more with them, up to Chaiten. There they decided to stay and decide what to do.

properties.name: El Amarillo
properties.description: She normally works as a taxi, like Uber but not through the application because no one uses that here. She often makes large distances like to Futalefu. Very chill and confident.

properties.name: La Junta
properties.description: A grandma with her nephew. But she is very young, around 50 and also does not feel like a grandma. She talks like a young person, also by the words she uses. She says most her her friends are the age of her daughter, around 30, they also go partying together. She used to work in a disco for many years, working from 22 to 6 in the morning, while having 4 kids. She lost 8 family members in the landslide of Villa Santa Lucia, including her mom. It was a crazy story and must have been so hard, she just accidentally wasn’t home and went to Futalefu, and when whe returned, half the village was gone. Her mom had a cafeteria and many travelers passed through there. When she died, she got condolences from all over the world. When we drove through Santa Lucia, she showed us where her house used to be. She has 8 butterflies tattooed on her hand, which represents the 8 people she lost. Villa Santa Lucia is named after the wife of Pinochet. Angelica met her and also Pinochet when she was young. She spoke really fondly of him, called him a simple man, a just and honest man. She said that he killed no one. But later she relativated that of course his orders killed people, but not himself. And she said that she likes to focus on the good things he did, like the carretera austral and the fact that there was almost no deliquencia when he was in power.

properties.name: La Junta
properties.description: We crossed paths again and since it was late, they offered to bring us to our camping spot.  We slept next to the river and just beside the bridge. Chill place, there were some young people partying but they were fun. The color of the water is amazing.

properties.name: Entrance Quelulat
properties.description: Sometimes the coincidences are crazy, they passed just when we started to hitchhike, so they offered to take us to the national park. There we realized that the entrance is very expensive, so we tried to continue to the hot springs

properties.name: Delfin Spot
properties.description: None car stopped, so we walked for almost one hour

properties.name: Laguna las Torres
properties.description: After walking almost one hour, we asked this French couple if they could bring us to the hot springs, because they are only accessible during low tide and it was already late. They accepted immediately and we left. They didn’t have seats in the back but we just sat on the bed. Unfortunately we arrived too late to the hot springs, so they offered to take us further up to their campspot

properties.name: Cruze por Aysen
properties.description: Young guy in a big van, he bought it to travel around. Calm, we did not talk much.

properties.name: Coyhaique
properties.description: We almost did not fit in with our bags, but he made it work. Saved us from the incoming rain and brought us to Coyhaique.

properties.name: Mirador Rio Simpson
properties.description: Arrived late so we just slept at the mirador de rio simpson, just under the platform. Not the cleanest spot, but with a great view and quiet.

properties.name: El Blanco
properties.description: Back of a truck, Amazing spot at the confluence of two rivers, camped on the beach, very calm. The French couple made a campfire and we roasted marshmallows

properties.name: Puerto Ibanez Playa
properties.description: The French couple texted me that they are camping close to town and invited me to join. It was very nice to see them again and we had a great evening getting to know each other and I was very intrigued to hear about their love story. They met when they were around 17, and Sophie was immediately in love, but it took Clemente 2 years to respond with the same feelings. They are married now and always wanted to make a big trip together, which is this one today. We camped again at the same spot, for the third time. But this time I camped in the front part, just under a small tree, very cozy. Clement caught the first fish of his life and we had an amazing dinner

properties.name: Chile Chico
properties.description: I went to Chile Chico to buy something from the pharmacy before crossing to Argentina

properties.name: Border Chile Chico
properties.description: After waiting for around 2-3h in Chile Chico, a guy in a pickup brought me to the border. He saved me, because from there it was much easier to continue

properties.name: La Ascencion
properties.description: Two Argentinian guys, going back from a visit in Chile Chico.

properties.name: Estancia la Ascencion
properties.description: A very beautiful free camping spot, with toilets and even hot showers, but you have to heat the water with an oven heated with wood. So someone always has to watch the fire while the other can take a shower. Had another great night with the French couple, nice talks about life and politics. We found out that we have very different political views, but that did and should not change the friendship.

properties.name: Rio Chico
properties.description: I could continue with my French friends, sitting on the back of the van on their bed, really comfortable. A very random camp in the middle of nowhere, quite windy but we could hide behind some bushes. We could even make a campfire and cooked on it. Unfortunately, Sophie lost her drone here.

properties.name: Gobernador, Gregores
properties.description: German couple, the most German guys I ever met. A bit uptight and boring, but cute. Brought me to the next town.

properties.name: Rio Coig
properties.description: it turns out that they go the same way as me, and when they drove past they stopped again and I ended up going another two days with them haha. It was amazing, I really like them.  We even went to see penguins on the way in the national park Monte Leon.  We camped in the middle of nowhere there is a little oasis, with a small river or lake with many birds. We saw flamingos, swans with black necks and many ducks. Very beautiful sunset.

properties.name: Police checkpoint
properties.description: Goodbye from the French couple :(

properties.name: Rio Gallego
properties.description: When arriving at the police stop, I met another hitchhiker that also hitchhiked boats one year after me, called Themis. We hitchhiked together and Pablo picked us up. He’s a middle aged man which just went trailrunning. He can do 100 miles in 30h, which is so impressive.

properties.name: Ferry Magellan Street
properties.description: I was so lucky that she stopped, she is coming from Buenos Aires and going back to her home in Rio Grande. We crossed the border together and also the ferry. She is very cute and friendly, talking about her family which lives far away. She is already retired but she used to be a math teacher. A typical mom, taking cute care of me

properties.name: Ferry Street Magellan
properties.description: The ferry is free for pedestrians

properties.name: Ushuaia
properties.description: On the ferry I talked to the other cars and had the luck to meet Sergio, going all the way to Ushuaia. We had a quiet and fast ride, arriving around 8pm in the evening to Ushuaia.

properties.name: Home of Martin
properties.description: I found a last minute couchsurfing host. Martin lives in a great apartment with view over the city. He is a retired police officer, but just 48 years old. He is gay, but was married and has two kids. He only started to live his true life around 10 years ago. I ended up staying 4 nights, after two nights also Themis joined, the hitchhiker I met in Rio Gallego.

properties.name: Ushuaia exit
properties.description: young mom of two kids, forgot something at home and she lives exactly at the city exit, so it was perfect for me. She’s an artist and works in the university. She also loves trailrunning and said I should try it, it gives a rush of adrenaline.

properties.name: Rio Grande
properties.description: older couple, but only together since 6 months. Offered me mate. She traveled a lot with her former partner, once 22k km in 3 months. She is originally from Chiloe.

properties.name: Rio Grande Exit
properties.description: young dad and his baby daughter. He agrees to take me to the other side of the city, but has to drop off Emma at the kindergarden. He works as a mechanic for Ford, said there are many foreign cars passing by here.

properties.name: Border San Sebastian
properties.description: Truck driver with a tooth missing, drinks lots of Mate and has Palos Santos in his truck. Very friendly and quiet. Brought me to the border

properties.name: Ferry Magellan Street
properties.description: Forest engineer, lives in Rio Gallegos. Also picked up a Russian hitchhiker, Andres. Lucas has a wood workshop but he had to close it because of the difficult economic situation. The Russian hitchhiker has a sad story, he lost both his parents and now recently also his brother, apparently in the war. So he left Russia and does not want to go back any time soon.

properties.name: Ferry Magellan Street
properties.description: Ferry is free for pedestrians

properties.name: Police checkpoint Rio Gallegos
properties.description: I asked around on the ferry and found Facundo to bring me a bit further than Rio Gallegos to a police checkpoint. He works as a salesman for glasses and travels all the country alone to visit different opticians. He is very flexible in his work and earns a lot (8000 dollars a month). He has a starlink in his car. When he heard that the Russian guy is on his way to Cordoba, we managed to find him and Lucas again in Rio Gallegos at his wood workshop and he also picked him up. He said he prefers to travel with company.

properties.name: Police checkpoint
properties.description: Arrived late and asked the police if I can put my tent close to the checkpoint, they did not mind. Cold night but calm.

properties.name: El Calafate Airport
properties.description: Elderly couple, sweet, they just bought a new car and want to make some kilometers. They are going to Calafate to pick up their son who is flying in from Cordoba.

properties.name: El Calafate
properties.description: a taxi driver, but made en exception for me and also two other hitchhikers we saw. He said that he also was traveling as a backpacker before so he wants to help.

properties.name: Hostal LeoLei
properties.description: Was in need of some shower and escape the cold, so I took a hostel. Met amazing people there, for example Finn who hiked from Esquel to El Chalten in 14 days apparently, but it’s hard to believe.

properties.name: El Calafate Exit
properties.description: Back of a pickup

properties.name: Glacier Perito Moreno
properties.description: From France, Nice. Very friendly, took 3 of us, because I met two French girls studying in Buenos Aires

properties.name: El Chalten
properties.description: Older Canadian couple, he is from Quebec and she is from China. They have been together for 20 years with no kids. They have a sweet relationship, she is taking pictures non-stop and he protests. She plans all the trip and he happily follows.

properties.name: El Chalten Refugio Hostel
properties.description: It was so cold so I took a hostel for one night.

properties.name: Gobernador Gregores
properties.description: saved me in El Chalten after hitchhiking for 4 hours with no success. I know Rosalie from Instagram and she is currently traveling with Simon, a Spanish guy in his van. The van has only two spots, so I sat in the back on the bed, disconnected from the drivers cabin and without windows. Simon built the van himself in 2019 and came back to travel with it. He is an architect but now mainly traveling. He likes to drive in the night, so we left around 7 and because of a very bad road and recent floodings, we arrived around 2am. We even had to put the snowchains on the car to get through the mud. But I was happy in the back with amazing starlink connection.

properties.name: Gobernador Gregores Balneario
properties.description: Amazing spot, next to the river and great to put a hammock. Spent the whole day with Simon and Rosalie and also the French couple who arrived here to make laundry. We did crepes together and enjoyed the good weather

properties.name: Perito Moreno
properties.description: After unsuccessfully hitchhiking for another 3h and meeting a French couple who tried the whole day, I asked them if I could go again with them. They left even later, around 10 pm and we arrived at 4am. But I slept amazingly in the back, even though there were maaaany holes in the road.  arrived at 4am, slept next to the lake next to some trees to avoid the wind. Calm but short night.

properties.name: Los Antiguos
properties.description: Such a sweet family, Antonio is the son and Dila the nephew. Felt so comfortable with them, the kids were not shy at all. I gave Antonio 5 Euros and he was very happy to have foreign currency. They told me that they normally don’t pick up Argentinians, just foreigners.

properties.name: Chile Chico border
properties.description: guy and his mom, going back to Chile after buying cheap cigarettes in Argentina.

properties.name: Chile Chico
properties.description: Two guys who offered to bring me to town without me even asking.

properties.name: El Blanco
properties.description: I asked around on the ferry and Selena said that her husband is waiting and they yes they can take me. Amelima is their two year old daughter. She is Argentinan and be from Chile. Calm ride, I was so thankful because the weather and the wind was crazy. Slept a second time in this nice spot, but now it was rainy, windy and cold. The river rose a lot over night, I was surprised. There was a quite annoying dog who tried to get into my tent.

properties.name: Coyhaique
properties.description: Father and son. Both simultaneously made the sign of the cross when we passed the San Sebastian sign, very synchronously haha. San Sebastián is the saint of the drivers

properties.name: Cruze
properties.description: works in the firewood business, brought me out of the town a bit.

properties.name: Cruze por Aysen
properties.description: he’s the boss of all cruz verde pharmacies in Chile South of Santiago. Travelled to Europe and also Switzerland. He told me about a story where they took the bus, and the controller just picked the of them to be controlled, and no one else, just for looking Latino.

properties.name: Cruze por Puerto Cisnes
properties.description: Works in something connected to construction, right now they are building some social housing for 17 families in Puerto Cisnes. Really chill guy, used to be a skater he told me. Really into rock music. Is the only one voting left in  his workmates, gets made fun of and called communist.

properties.name: Puyuhuapi
properties.description: Saved me from a 2h wait in the rain, and also two other hitchhikers that just arrived. They were also a middle aged couple, they didn’t have a bus back from Puerto Cisnes. Fun mood in the car, Mabel laughed a lot. They actually just wanted to see the salto de condor, but drive past it and turned around, which was my luck, otherwise they would not have driven by me

properties.name: Hostal Juanita
properties.description: Took another hostel because of the rain and cold. Even my own room, luxury

properties.name: La Junta
properties.description: Another Rodrigo, works in a lodge for fishing. Huge pickup. His season is almost over, then they close and he’s off for the winter, but still gets paid.

properties.name: Chaiten
properties.description: another German haha, what a coincidence. Talked a lot, seemed a but lonely. Is traveling with his camping trailer for the first time, his two kids accompanied him at first but got bored and left. Now he’s alone, he kept saying that’s it’s better because he’s more free but at the same time was complaining how lonely it was. He can’t cook, so he calls his wife and she gives him instructions (for a sandwich as well haha). Is really left wing but also huge fan of Russia and Putin. Interesting combination.

properties.name: Chaiten Beach
properties.description: A Dutch couple asked me to drive their van to the beach because they drank some beers

properties.name: Hot springs

properties.name: Hornopiren
properties.description: Brought me to the town center, recognized me because she worked on the ferry the day before

properties.name: Puelche
properties.description: Working in the wood industry, in Contao. Is selling land there, 9000 euros for half a hectare. Also gave me the contact of a geomatics firm here.

properties.name: Puerto Montt
properties.description: Germans living in Chile since 5 years. Dad and daugther plus boyfriend. Jens cannot speak Spanish at all

properties.name: Home Gabito
properties.description: Stayed here for a bit more then a week

properties.name: Refugio Puyehue
